claim: Physical substrate is necessary for information generation and integration, and thus for conscious processing.
falsifier: The claim can be tested by comparing systems with and without appropriate physical substrates for their capacity to generate integrated information and exhibit consciousness indicators.

conditions: the system must have a physical substrate capable of information generation and integration
exclusions: limited to the Integrated Information Theory (IIT) perspective as reviewed

title: Physical substrate–information generation and integration mechanism

claim: Hierarchical multi-agent structure (coarse prescreening followed by fine ranking) increases the likelihood of identifying a chemically reasonable first candidate, especially at low and medium reasoning effort.
falsifier: The claim can be tested by comparing the first-candidate accuracy of a hierarchical multi-agent system against a single-agent baseline at varying reasoning effort levels.

conditions: CO adsorption on Cu-surface adatoms and M–N–C catalysts
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the specific hierarchical architectures studied (triage-ranking, triage-forms) and the two chemical domains; transfer to other architectures or domains is unestablished.

title: Hierarchical multi-agent structure for Likelihood of identifying
